question.text: Which statement correctly describes the concept of 'contango' and 'backwardation' in futures markets?

answer.text: Contango: futures price above spot price (normal for financial assets). Backwardation: futures price below spot price (common in commodities with convenience yield)
Contango: futures price below spot price. Backwardation: futures price above spot price
Both terms refer to the daily mark-to-market adjustment in futures positions
Contango and backwardation only apply to commodity futures, not financial derivatives

explanation.text: The Logic: Contango occurs when the futures price is above the spot price — typical for financial assets where the cost of carry (interest) makes futures costlier. Backwardation occurs when futures trade below spot — common in commodities where holding the physical asset offers a convenience yield exceeding storage and financing costs. The Trap: The definitions are often reversed in error. Contango means a futures premium (above spot); backwardation means a futures discount (below spot). Although backwardation is more common in commodities, it can occur in any market and is not the same as daily mark-to-market. Note: Rewrote the malformed second option as a complete, distinct distractor (contango = futures below spot; backwardation = futures above spot); distributor/cross-exam framing removed.
